findings: Every merge cites a charter goal (G1, G2 or G3), and the diffs I read match the goals they cite. None touches pyproject.toml, uv.lock, .github or the deployment files, and no dependency was added.

G1/G2 look met on the code as it stands. I ran `python3 -m evals.offline_eval` on a /tmp copy of the repo using the system Python. It printed TOTAL 1.000 on all five metrics. The arming baseline in evals/baseline.json is 0.815 posting-shape, 0.765 aggregator-drop, 1.0 location, 0.429 staleness and 0.571 dedup. So nothing regressed and the two required metrics improved.

Risk of overfitting and a moving target: T-0026 changed what the harness scores (only POSTING-shaped pages now survive replay) and removed the old test `test_replay_keeps_non_aggregator_index_page`. T-0027 then re-froze the corpus, which was labelled by the same agents. The change is documented and the baseline was re-derived against the arming revision b6da8dd, so I don't count it as weakening a test. But the 58-record corpus now scores 1.000 everywhere and has no room left to show further G2 gains.

Process churn is the main problem: 915 agent runs, $82.04 and 46 sandbox denials for 29 merges. At least 14 tasks were parked and re-issued, mostly because update_task changes to depends_on never took effect in the tree and because 'planned task never reached the backlog'. The runner or planner needs fixing.

The most recent G3 merges are in scope: T-0052 missing-profile message plus requeue fix, T-0056/T-0057 naming errors in empty-scan messages, and T-0055/T-0060 exact-text assertions. T-0060 strengthens assertions from substring checks to exact equality. Four merges only edit the README. That is allowed but thin.
Minor code smell in T-0057: the orchestrator reads `last_search_error` from shared crawler state through getattr after `tools.invoke`. That is only safe while searches run one at a time.

Assumption, recorded: I could not run `uv run pytest -q` or `uv run python -m evals.offline_eval`. uv needed to download packages and network access is disabled for me, and I did not try to get around that. So the 182-passed/1-skipped baseline is not re-verified. The metric table above came from the system Python.
digest: The work stayed on charter. All 29 merges map to a goal, and the diffs do what their tasks say. On the offline harness, every metric now scores 1.000, up from the arming baseline (posting-shape 0.81, aggregator-drop 0.76, staleness 0.43, dedup 0.57), and nothing regressed. The G3 work on the bot's messages covers four things: every job message says why it matched, a durable ledger stops repeat notifications, failed scans and failed deliveries now produce a message naming the problem, and users with incomplete setup are told what is missing. Tests were made stricter, not weaker. No dependency or deployment changes. Two concerns. First, the harness is saturated: the agents changed its scoring rules and grew its corpus themselves, and it now scores perfectly, so it can't show further gains. Second, the process was wasteful: 915 runs and $82 for 29 merges, with over a dozen tasks parked and re-issued because dependency updates never took effect. I could not run the full test suite (uv needs network access, which is disabled here), so the test count is unconfirmed. Drift is low; no pause needed.
